body: NVIDIA's data-center revenue was visible and compounding years before ChatGPT: $339M in FY16, $1.93B in FY18 and $10.6B in FY22. After 2023, most of the stock's gain came from **earnings growth, not multiple expansion**. Forward P/E actually fell from above 40 to the high teens or low 20s by 2026 as earnings exploded. Holders had to sit through **two drawdowns of 50%+** (2018 and 2022).
title: multibagger_case_studies › Takeaway

body: Nearly every great long-term stock suffered drawdowns of 50–95% on the way up. Knowing to "hold winners" is easy. Holding through a 90% fall, which needs a 9x rebound to get back to even, is what separates outcomes. The popular Fidelity "best investors were dead or forgot" study is a **MYTH**: no such study has been found.

body:
`case_study:credit-suisse-2023` | 2023-03-19 | tickers: US-CS | confidence: verified

Credit Suisse's share price was ~CHF 70+ in 2007 and ~CHF 0.76 equivalent in the UBS rescue on 19 Mar 2023 (UBS paid CHF 3 bn in stock; ~CHF 16 bn of AT1 bonds written to zero while shareholders got something -- inverting the usual hierarchy). Path: Mozambique 'tuna bonds' (2013-16), spying scandal (2019), Greensill supply-chain funds ($10 bn frozen, Mar 2021), Archegos loss ($5.5 bn, Mar-Apr 2021), repeated CEO/chair changes, a 2022 strategic overhaul and CHF 4 bn rights issue; Q4 2022 client outflows of ~CHF 110 bn; 14 Mar 2023 annual report disclosed 'material weaknesses' in controls (PwC); 15 Mar Saudi National Bank (top holder) said it would 'absolutely not' add capital; SNB liquidity line failed to stop the run. Visible flags: (1) CDS spreads blowing out in Oct 2022; (2) serial risk-management failures = culture, not bad luck; (3) price-to-tangible-book ~0.2-0.3 'cheapness' for years; (4) management turnover; (5) wealth-management outflows; (6) auditor material-weakness opinion. Lesson: a bank trading far below book for years with repeated scandals is a value trap -- the discount is the market pricing hidden losses and run risk. AT1s are equity-like in a crisis.

**Lesson:** Persistent deep discount + scandals = value trap
**Spotted early by:** CDS market; depositors

`insight:flag-override-template` · verified

HOW TO USE: every flag that fires on a candidate gets one row, written down before a decision, and saved as a decision/analysis record (L10). Hard disqualifiers (fraud signals, auditor exit citing information denial, related-party diversion, fake-cash signals) are NOT overridable by this template. ROW FORMAT: FLAG (metric, value, years) | CONTEXT QUESTIONS | EVIDENCE THAT CLEARS (must come from outside the company's own P&L where possible) | EVIDENCE THAT CONFIRMS | VERDICT (cleared / open / confirmed) | WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND | REVIEW DATE. EXAMPLES: High P/E -> Is EPS depressed? Reverse DCF implied growth vs reinvestment x ROIC? P/E vs own median? -> clears: implied growth below demonstrated, unit data shows runway; confirms: P/E >2x own median, slowing unit growth. Negative FCF/low CFO -> What asset is being built? Whose working capital? -> clears: own inventory/sovereign debtor/high-ROCE capex; confirms: receivables to related or unknown parties, WC sign contradicts model. Rising debt -> Lease, GML, govt dues or bank/CP? Tenor? -> clears: lease/GML/long-tenor; confirms: short funds long, debt + negative CFO. Pledge -> six checks (insight:flag-pledge-severity). High ROE/ROCE -> DuPont; CFO/PAT; peer gap; lender growth vs system. Cash pile -> yield, location, cash+debt. Receivables -> counterparty, ageing, related-party share. Losses/dilution -> unit economics; price x purpose x buyer; per-share outcome. Low margin -> ROCE and WC days. RULES: a flag cleared only by management's explanation stays OPEN; if 3+ flags stay open, no position without a variant view; record false alarms and missed traps afterwards to calibrate the checklist.

- **H1, fresh:** **PROVEN-fresh** if the top-quintile mean excess **net of 1%** at 63d is > 0, **and** either the
  week-clustered t on the net figure is > 3 or its 95% cluster-bootstrap CI excludes zero.
  **H1, re-run:** **REPLICATES** if the 2022–25 quarter-level net-of-1% mean is > 0 with t > 3 or a 95% CI that excludes
  zero.
  **H1 is "supported" only if PROVEN-fresh and REPLICATES both hold.** Fresh alone counts as "fresh pass, no replication"
  and re-run alone as "not proven OOS". Neither half is called an edge.
- **H2:** the statistic is the contrast **D = mean excess(top ∩ ann_ret > 0) − mean excess(top ∩ ann_ret ≤ 0)** at 63d,
  using fresh 2026 events only. H2 is supported if D > 0 and (week-clustered t > 3 or the 95% cluster-bootstrap CI of D
  excludes zero) **and** the filtered top quintile's net-of-1% mean is above the unfiltered one. 2022–25 D is
  replication only.
- **H3:** supported if the bottom-quintile mean excess at 63d in 2026 is **≤ −1%** and (week-clustered t < −3 or the
  95% CI upper bound < 0). No cost adjustment applies, because avoiding a stock costs nothing.
- **H4:** descriptive only.
- **Everything else is exploratory:** 21d and 126d, T−B, the consolidated-only subset, by-quarter results, the Sep-26
  21d result, deciles and mcap splits.
- No hypothesis, horizon, filter or statistic will be added to the verdict after results are seen. Deviations go in
  the log below with a date and a reason, written before the affected numbers are computed where possible.

body:
1. **Garbage in.** Scenario probabilities, ROIIC and exit P/E are opinions. The tool makes them explicit and scoreable; it does not make them right.
2. **The cost-of-equity convention dominates the DCF for Indian stocks** (§2.3.1). Treat DCF value as "what the cash flows justify at our hurdle", not as a price target. The sensitivity table shows the spread: at 10.5% CoE, VMM's base value rises by ~45%.
3. **The EPS path is approximate.** EPS scales with NOPAT + recurring other income, and treasury income is held flat. Buybacks, dilution and changes in interest are not modelled; SBC dilution must be inside the margin.
4. **One growth path per scenario**, with linear fades. Cyclicals (Cummins' margin cycle) need a cycle-aware base year. Use a normalised margin as `nopat_margin`, not the peak.
5. **Base rates are weak.** The India class is survivors-only and bull-biased, the US class is IPOs over 3 years, and blow-up rates are unknown everywhere. A **stage-1 task** (Pi + Kite/NSE bhavcopy + delisting lists) is to compute 5-year outcome distributions by size bucket and starting-P/E bucket, from several start dates, including delisted firms.
6. **The 5-year paper calls resolve slowly** (first in Nov-2031). Stage 7 also needs faster feedback, so each live card should add one or two 6–12 month calls (for example on a kill criterion or a reverse-DCF growth check). The v1 card does not generate those automatically.
7. **The PEAD gate depends on the live tracker** (`research_notes/Backtests/india_pead_live/`). Until a company has a computed SUE quintile, the gate reads "unknown, does not block". It is not wired to the tracker's CSV yet.
8. **The credibility gate needs ≥5 promises per category and a peer median (L18).** Without both, it is shown and ignored.
9. **Liquidity cap** needs ADV and portfolio value in the same money units. If they are not supplied, it is skipped (shown as n/a).
10. **US temperature has no market-level base rate on file.** The Nifty bands come from `insight:india-valuation-forward-returns` (data mostly before 2015).
11. **Not wired to memdb metrics yet.** Inputs are typed by hand. Next: a `--from-memdb TICKER` loader once stage-1 snapshots land in `memdb metric`.
